chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) was saying: 'It would astound me, the man, if his forbearance comes across him during his anger'.

key_terms.حِلْمٌ: Forbearance, gentleness, or mildness; a quality of calmness and patience.
key_terms.يُدْرِكُهُ: It overtakes him or comes upon him.

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when a person's forbearance overcomes them during anger?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) expressed admiration for a man whose natural disposition of forbearance (hilm) manifests even in the heat of anger, highlighting the virtue of self-control where patience becomes an inherent trait rather than a forced struggle. This narration, found in al-Kafi's chapter on Forbearance, underscores the Shia emphasis on *hilm* as a spiritual refinement that tempers the soul's natural passions, reflecting the prophetic ideal of controlling one's temper as a sign of true strength and divine proximity. The chain of transmission through Zurarah and Ibn Bukayr connects this teaching to the core companions of the Imams, reinforcing its authenticity and practical relevance in daily conduct.
